domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, manager decision, and potential cancellation.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Each policy governs how many days employees receive, whether manager approval is required, and any notice-period constraints.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. Tracks employment lifecycle and reporting hierarchy (managerId). Employment status gates leave eligibility.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Deducted on approval; restored on cancellation.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type maps to a LeavePolicy that defines its rules. The feature scope covers annual, sick, and emergency; unpaid, maternity, and paternity are defined for completeness.

modules.name: leave-type
owns: LeaveType enum (ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY, UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY)

modules.name: leave-request-status
owns: LeaveRequestStatus enum (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Domain Primitives — leave-type & leave-request-status
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency enums that every other module references. Must exist first.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Employee module
recommended_phases.rationale: Employee model, EmploymentStatus enum, and repository interface — needed by leave-request, leave-balance, notification, and leave. No dependency on other leave modules.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: leave-policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on leave-type. Defines accrual rules, max balances, and approval rules per leave type.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: leave-request module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-type, leave-request-status, and employee. Model + repository interface for the leave request aggregate.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: leave-balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-type, employee, and leave-policy. Model, repository interface, service interface, and service implementation for balance tracking.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6: Cross-cutting — audit-log & notification
recommended_phases.rationale: Audit-log has no leave-module deps. Notification depends only on employee. Both are consumed by the leave orchestrator.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 7: leave module (orchestrator)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all modules above. Contains ILeaveService, LeaveService (orchestrates apply/approve/reject/cancel with balance checks, policy validation, audit recording, and notifications), controller, routes, and validation schemas.

architecture_md_update:
## Leave Management Module

### Domain Entities

- **LeaveRequest** — Represents an employee's leave application. Lifecycle: `DRAFT` → `SUBMITTED` → (`APPROVED` | `REJECTED`); `APPROVED` may transition to `CANCELLED`.
- **LeavePolicy** — Rules and entitlements per leave type. Lifecycle: `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`.
- **Employee** — Employee record with reporting hierarchy. Lifecycle: `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, `TERMINATED`.
- **LeaveBalance** — Tracks entitlement, consumption, and remaining days per employee-policy-fiscal year. Lifecycle: `ACTIVE`, `EXHAUSTED`, `FROZEN`.
- **LeaveType** — Enum: `annual`, `sick`, `emergency`, `unpaid`, `maternity`, `paternity`.

### Business Rules

- **BR-001** — Balance sufficiency: before approval, `remainingDays` must cover the leave duration; otherwise reject.
- **BR-002** — Manager approval gate: if `requiresManagerApproval` is true, only the employee's manager can approve/reject. No manager → auto-approve.
- **BR-003** — Minimum notice: if `minimumNoticeDays` is set, submission date to `startDate` must meet it; blocks `DRAFT` → `SUBMITTED`.
- **BR-004** — No retroactive leave: `startDate` ≥ submission date.
- **BR-005** — Date range validity: `endDate` ≥ `startDate`.
- **BR-006** — Balance deduction on approval: atomically increment `usedDays` and decrement `remainingDays`.
- **BR-007** — Balance restoration on cancellation: atomically decrement `usedDays` and increment `remainingDays`.

### Module Boundaries

```
leave (orchestrator)
 ├── leave-request
 │    ├── leave-type
 │    ├── leave-request-status
 │    └── employee
 ├── leave-balance
 │    ├── leave-type
 │    ├── employee
 │    └── leave-policy
 ├── leave-policy → leave-type
 ├── audit-log (no leave deps)
 ├── notification → employee
 └── employee
```

- **leave-type** — `LeaveType` enum.
- **leave-request-status** — `LeaveRequestStatus` enum (`DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED`).
- **employee** — `Employee` model, `EmploymentStatus` enum, `IEmployeeRepository`.
- **leave-policy** — `LeavePolicy` model, `ILeavePolicyRepository`.
- **leave-balance** — `LeaveBalance` model, `BalanceStatus` enum, `ILeaveBalanceRepository`, `ILeaveBalanceService`, `LeaveBalanceService`.
- **leave-request** — `LeaveRequest` model, `ILeaveRequestRepository`.
- **audit-log** — `AuditLog` model, `IAuditLogRepository`, `IAuditLogService`, `AuditLogService`.
- **notification** — `INotificationService`, `NotificationService`.
- **leave** — `ILeaveService`, `LeaveService`, `LeaveController`, routes, validation schemas.

### Data Model (Conceptual)

| Table | Key Fields | Notes |
|-------|------------|-------|
| `employees` | id, employee_number, email, manager_id, employment_status | Unique on employee_number, email. Indexes on manager_id, department, status. |
| `leave_types` | id, code | Unique on code. |
| `leave_policies` | id, leave_type_id, is_active | FK to leave_types. Indexes on leave_type_id, is_active. |
| `leave_requests` | id, employee_id, leave_type_id, status, start_date, end_date, approved_by | FKs to employees (employee, approver) and leave_types. Indexes on employee_id, status, leave_type_id, date range, approved_by. |
| `leave_balances` | id, employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year, status | FKs to employees, leave_policies. Unique on (employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year). Indexes on employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year. |
| `audit_logs` | id, entity_type, entity_id, action, performed_by, performed_at | FK to employees. Composite index on (entity_type, entity_id). Indexes on performed_by, performed_at, action. |

### Implementation Notes

- **Stack**: TypeScript, Fastify, PostgreSQL, React Native (frontend), modular-monolith.
- **Golden Principles**:
  - GP-001: All data access through repository interfaces (`ILeaveRequestRepository`, etc.).
  - GP-002: Every state change writes an audit record via `IAuditLogService`.
  - GP-003: Input validation at Fastify route boundary using `leaveValidationSchemas`.
  - GP-005: RBAC enforced in routes — employees manage own requests; managers approve/reject team requests.
  - GP-006: Async error handling with try/catch in services and controllers.
- **Phases**: Build in 7 phases — domain primitives first, then employee, policy, request, balance, cross-cutting services, and finally the leave orchestrator.
- **Transactions**: Balance deduction (BR-006) and restoration (BR-007) must run within a database transaction to ensure atomicity.
sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team-level queries; employment_status: filter active/inactive/terminated; department: department-scoped queries
table leave_types | fields: id, code, label, created_at | pk: id | indexes: code: unique lookup by leave type code

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: filter policies by leave type; is_active: filter active policies; policy_name: lookup by policy name

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list all leave requests for an employee; status: filter by status (SUBMITTED for manager approval queues, APPROVED for calendar views); leave_type_id: filter requests by leave type; start_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: find all requests approved by a specific manager

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up balances for a specific employee; policy_id: look up balances by policy; fiscal_year: filter balances by fiscal year; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint to prevent duplicate balance records per employee-policy-year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: look up all audit records for a specific entity; performed_by: look up all actions by a specific user; performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports; action: filter by action type
